name: SampleSheet generator
tagline: Builds a BCL Convert v2 sample sheet for a NextSeq 2000 run, checking sample names and index collisions across the whole run as you type.
who: Whoever plans a run and has to be sure two samples cannot demultiplex into each other.

notes.use:
One web page and nothing else — no install, no server, no black window. It also works with no internet: save `index.html` and double-click it.

It is the **authority on indexes**. Nothing else in the platform decides whether two barcodes can be sequenced together, and nothing else should: the Hamming distance rule, the mixed-length reconciliation and the padding table were hard-won, and they live here.

change: Sharing plates with the whole lab

change.what: Add an index plate for yourself
change.manual: In the app: **➕ Manage index plates** at the bottom. Upload the vendor's `.csv`, `.tsv` or `.xlsx`, or paste the table. The plate is saved in your browser and is available immediately — to you only.

change.what: Publish an index plate to the whole lab
change.manual: Click **⬇ shared_plates.json (for git)**, which merges the lab's existing plates with yours, then commit that file to the root of the repository. Once GitHub Pages redeploys, every user sees the plate as `lab · <name>`. ProjectHub reads the same file, so the plate reaches the library-prep dropdowns too. The file is currently empty, and correctly so — nobody has added a plate yet.

change.what: Change a built-in kit or add read-length defaults
change.manual: Edit `Samplesheet_generator/samplesheet_data.json`, then `python build.py` to regenerate `index.html`. Never hand-edit `index.html` — it is generated.

quick: Open the app in a browser. There is nothing to install.
Run setup: run name and cycles. Index cycles are detected from the chosen kit.
Add one project per customer or application, each with its own index kit and plate.
Type or bulk-paste samples: Sample ID, barcode or well, project.
Validation runs live across the WHOLE run, not per project.
Fix anything red — duplicate names, wells, or indexes closer than Hamming 3.
Copy for BaseSpace, or download the sample sheet .csv.
Download the Records .csv too: it is the archive of what was actually loaded.
